title: Cumulative Frequency, Quartiles and Box-and-Whisker Plots
seo_title: Sec 4 Cumulative frequency and box plots Worksheets: Free Secondary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: quartiles and percentiles; range and interquartile range as measures of spread; analysis and interpretation of cumulative frequency diagrams and box-and-whisker plots
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 maths worksheets on quartiles, interquartile range, percentiles, cumulative frequency tables and curves, box-and-whisker plots and comparing data. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: IQR = upper quartile − lower quartile: the spread of the middle half.
key_sub: On a cumulative frequency curve, read across from n/4, n/2 and 3n/4, then down.
body_html:
How it works

  • Sort the data. The median splits it in half; the lower quartile Q1 and upper quartile Q3 are the medians of the lower and upper halves.
  • Interquartile range = Q3 − Q1. It measures the spread of the middle 50%.
  • On a cumulative frequency curve for n values, read across from n/2 for the median, n/4 for Q1 and 3n/4 for Q3, then read down.
  • A box-and-whisker plot shows the minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. A smaller IQR means more consistent data.
Example

Find the IQR of 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, 15, 20.

Lower half 3, 5, 7, 8: Q₁ = 6

Upper half 9, 12, 15, 20: Q₃ = 13.5

Answer: 7.5

Example

A cumulative frequency curve shows 80 students. Where do you read the upper quartile?

3/4 × 80 = 60

Answer: Across from 60, then down

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to sort the data first.
  • Reading the cumulative frequency axis instead of the value axis for the answer.
  • Using n/2 instead of n/4 for the lower quartile.
  • Comparing medians when the question asks which data is more consistent (spread).

faq.q: How do you find quartiles from a list?
faq.a: Sort the data and find the median. Q₁ is the median of the lower half and Q₃ is the median of the upper half.

faq.q: How do you read the median from a cumulative frequency curve?
faq.a: Find half the total on the cumulative frequency axis, go across to the curve, then down to the value axis.

faq.q: What does a box-and-whisker plot show?
faq.a: The minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum. The box holds the middle 50% of the data.

faq.q: How do you compare two box plots?
faq.a: Compare the medians to see which is higher on average, and the interquartile ranges to see which is more consistent.
